normative_extracts.quote: The Cache-Control header field is used to specify directives for caches along the request/response chain.
no-cache allows a response to be stored in a cache, but requires validation with the origin server before each reuse.

engine_internals.mechanism_summary: Evaluates Cache-Control freshness lifetimes and ETag validators before issuing network bytes, controlling disk cache reuse and bfcache eligibility.

production_failures.symptom: HTML shell serves stale hashed JS chunk URLs after a deployment, causing 404s
production_failures.root_cause: index.html was served with max-age=3600 without no-cache, so browsers reused the old HTML pointing to deleted chunk hashes.
production_failures.mitigation: Serve HTML with Cache-Control: no-cache (or max-age=0, must-revalidate) and hashed assets with max-age=31536000, immutable.

production_failures.symptom: bfcache hit rate drops to 0% across authenticated or marketing routes
production_failures.root_cause: Global middleware emitted Cache-Control: no-store on all document responses, which disqualifies pages from bfcache.
production_failures.mitigation: Use Cache-Control: private, no-cache for personalized HTML and reserve no-store strictly for sensitive post-logout views.
